title: A bill posted before the release is moved at Close after it
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use the production test account.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, billable, whose special-order part's vendor bill of $125.00 was posted to Cost of Parts before the release.
custom_steps:
1. After the release, make work order 1 internal by moving it to an internal customer.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 shows the "Internal" badge.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation shows the special order as moved from Cost of Parts.

Step 3:

  • The work order is Closed.

Step 4:

  • A reclass entry moves $125.00 from Cost of Parts to the category's account.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R4: “When a vendor bill was posted to Cost of Parts (or a category account) and the work order later becomes internal or no charge, Close adds a reclass journal entry: debit the mapped expense account, credit the account the bill line was posted to, for that bill's lines. When a vendor bill was posted to one expense account and the work order closes under the other classification, Close adds a reclass from the account the bill line was posted to, to the work order's mapped account; no reclass when both resolve to the same account. When a vendor bill was posted to an expense account and the work order becomes billable, invoicing adds the reverse entry: debit the account the bill would post to today, credit that expense account.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 4875 (TP-633): “Bills emitted before the version raise carry no category, so Close reclasses them as S7-R4 bills. Nothing is lost across the cut-over.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
